title: The Whisky Label Compliance Review | Craft Beer School
desc: How a whisky label compliance review works in India: what gets checked, who signs off, the state layer and the print and line checks after approval.
teaser: One wrong line on a whisky label can stop a launch in a state or pull stock off shelves. The review exists to catch it first.
standfirst: Every whisky label sold in India has to satisfy national food and packaging rules, state excise rules and the company's own standards. This guide explains how a label review works at process level and who checks what.
sections:
A whisky label is a legal document as well as a piece of design. It declares what the product is, how strong it is, how much is in the bottle, who made it and where it may be sold. Mistakes are expensive. A label that fails approval delays a launch in a state. A label printed wrongly after approval can mean relabelling stock under excise supervision or withdrawing it.

A compliance review is the structured check that happens before artwork is approved and again before printing. This guide describes the process. Rules vary by state and change, so teams must work from the current regulations and take legal advice. It is not legal advice.
The layers of rules a label must meet

In India a spirits label sits under several layers at once.

  • Food safety rules. FSSAI's standards for alcoholic beverages set product definitions and labelling requirements, including the declared alcohol content and statutory warnings.
  • Packaging and weights rules. Legal metrology rules require declarations such as net quantity, maximum retail price where applicable, the manufacturer or packer's name and address, date of manufacture or packing and consumer care details.
  • State excise rules. Each state registers labels for sale within it, may require state-specific text and controls excise adhesive labels or holograms.
  • Company and industry codes. Responsible marketing standards that often go further than the law.

Our guide to state labelling rules for spirits in India covers the state layer.
What reviewers check on the artwork

A thorough review works through the label line by line.

  • Product name and category. Does the product meet the definition of whisky it claims? Does it meet any sub-category it names, such as malt or blended?
  • Alcohol content. Declared as % ABV and matching the bottling specification, commonly 42.8% for mainstream Indian whisky.
  • Net quantity. In ml, matching the bottle size, such as 750, 375 or 180 ml.
  • Age statement. If shown, it must reflect the youngest whisky in the blend, not the oldest or an average.
  • Claims. Words such as small batch, single cask or a cask finish must be backed by production records. No health claims at all.
  • Statutory warnings and mandatory text. Present, legible and at the required size.
  • State text and codes. Correct for the state on this version of the label.

Our guide to whisky label terms explains the vocabulary.

Good reviews involve several functions, each owning its part. Regulatory or legal checks the mandatory content and claims. Quality or the blender checks that strength, age and liquid descriptions match production records. Marketing owns the design and brand language. Supply chain checks that the dimensions, barcode and print specification suit the bottle and the labeller.

Record each sign-off against a specific artwork version number. Most label errors that reach the market come from a late change approved on an old version, not from a misunderstanding of the rules.
After approval: print and line checks

Approval is not the end. The printer's proof must be checked against the approved artwork, not against memory. At the bottling line, the first labelled bottles of every run are checked against the approved sample: correct state version, batch code, strength and position.

On a line that switches between state labels for the same liquid, this first-off check is the step that stops a pallet of bottles labelled for one state being sent to another. It takes two minutes and saves days of relabelling.

Keep a label file for every SKU and state: approved artwork with version, sign-offs, registration or approval reference and the date it lapses or renews. Many state registrations follow the excise year, so a calendar of renewal dates by state avoids discovering in April that a label can no longer be sold.

Price changes deserve a line in the same file. In states where the maximum retail price is printed on the label, a price revision means new artwork, a new review and a plan for old stock still in the channel. Our guide to how MRP changes work for spirits in India covers that process.

Take your best selling SKU and gather every live state version of its label. Lay them side by side and check alcohol content, net quantity, warnings and age statement on each. Any difference that is not explained by a state rule is a question for the next review meeting.
faqs: What must a whisky label in India show?

Typically the product name, alcohol content, net quantity, manufacturer details, statutory warnings and state-specific text, under FSSAI, legal metrology and state excise rules. Check current regulations for the full list.
What does an age statement on whisky mean?
It refers to the youngest whisky in the bottle. A blend labelled 12 years old contains no whisky younger than twelve years.
Who should sign off a whisky label?
Regulatory or legal, quality or the blender, marketing and supply chain, each against a specific artwork version.
